content: Due to the potential for statins to cause significant adverse reactions in nursing infants, women who require treatment with atorvastatin should be advised against breastfeeding their infants. The safety and efficacy of atorvastatin in pediatric patients aged 10 to 17 years with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia have been evaluated in a controlled clinical trial lasting six months. This trial included adolescent boys and postmenarchal girls. Patients treated with atorvastatin exhibited an adverse event profile that was generally similar to that observed in patients receiving a placebo. The most frequently reported adverse events in both groups, regardless of causality, were infections. Doses of atorvastatin exceeding 20 mg have not been studied in this specific patient population. Adolescent females undergoing atorvastatin therapy should be counseled on the use of appropriate contraceptive methods.
